title: Neurotransmitter-aware spatial communication
question: Does a neurotransmitter/neuropeptide-aware, replicate-consistent spatial method recover canonical neural interactions and replicate across donors better than a generic database and a non-spatial consensus method?
notes: The canonical list was fixed in run.py before any results were inspected; it is small and textbook-level, so recall is a sanity check rather than a comprehensive benchmark.
LIANA is non-spatial (cluster-level) and uses its own consensus resource; its significance threshold here (magnitude_rank < 0.05) follows the LIANA documentation's suggested cut-off.
DLPFC classes come from NeuroSTIAS annotation of Visium spots (mixtures), so receiver/sender classes are dominant-class approximations.
